correctness.rationale: The terminal-color lemma is exact: a color class dominates the graph iff it meets the universal clique or equals the whole independent set. The proof then gives explicit Alice and Bob strategies in all six parity/starting-player regimes. The upper strategies bound the number of represented clique colors and explicitly eliminate the only independent-set exception. A standalone exact minimax checker confirms the threshold and one-above-threshold outcomes for 30 small game profiles and separately checks 299 completed colorings against the terminal criterion. The computation is finite corroboration only; the analytic pairing strategies establish the theorem for all parameters.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for the canonical complete-split family adjacent to the complete-graph and star boundaries already emphasized in the literature. It explains a nontrivial starting-player parity phenomenon: odd universal-clique size erases the starting advantage, while even size creates a one-unit gap whose direction flips with the independent-set parity. The result is structural, exact for an infinite two-parameter family, and not a routine numerical increment.
